method: BRREG pages rendered at 1728x2312, company pages at 1653x{2140,2338,2339,2340}. Image size extracted via fitz.extract_image() — zero pixel analysis needed for source split.

results.type_accuracy: 69% (33/48) — BRREG types from positional order, company types from silhouette features
results.cost: $0 (no API calls, no ML model, ~2ms per page)

brreg_page_order: p4: balanse (second page, IF n_brreg >= 6) OR noter

company_type_accuracy_breakdown.signatur: 2/5 correct — sparse signatur pages misclassified as noter
company_type_accuracy_breakdown.noter: 6/10 correct — confused with revisjonsberetning when text-heavy
company_type_accuracy_breakdown.resultatregnskap: 0/1 correct — company P&L looks identical to noter in pixels
company_type_accuracy_breakdown.balanse: 0/2 correct — company BS looks identical to noter in pixels

production_architecture.step_1: Extract image dimensions per page via fitz — split into brreg/company sections (100% accurate, $0)
production_architecture.step_2: Assign BRREG types by positional order (generell_info→resultatregnskap→balanse→noter)
production_architecture.step_3: Pass brreg_last_page to Gemini extract_pdf() as manifest input — prevents hallucinated company values
production_architecture.step_4: Gemini handles company section type assignment (it reads text, which is the only way to distinguish company P&L from noter)
production_architecture.cost_saving: Eliminates classify_pdf() call ($0.0003/entity) by providing brreg_last_page for free. Gemini extraction ($0.0012) still needed for actual data extraction.

key_insight: The previous silhouette experiment showed 75% source accuracy from pixel analysis. The actual discriminator was trivial: BRREG renders pages at a fixed 1728x2312 resolution. Company attachments are scanned at different resolutions. This is metadata, not pixels.

2338.note: audit report + signatur from same scan batch

company_sub_sizes.interpretation: Height variation within company section corresponds to physical document origin (separate scans), not content type. Audit reports (revisjonsberetning) are consistently scanned at different height than financial statements. This gives a partial but useful signal: non-2340 company pages are never P&L/BS/noter.

refined_classifier.1653x2340: company financial content — needs Gemini for type

company_sub_sizes.production_value: Image dimensions provide: (1) perfect brreg/company split, (2) partial company sub-typing — audit reports identifiable by height in most entities. The brreg_last_page boundary plus audit-report identification eliminates classify_pdf entirely for the extraction prompt. Gemini only needs to distinguish P&L vs BS vs noter within the 2340-height pages.
